title: Tight Bounds for Tight Links: Ropelength of T(Q,Q) torus links
summary: Ropelength, L, is a parameter characterizing the minimum contour length of a knot or link. There exist upper and lower bounds on ropelength with respect to crossing number, C, including a universal lower bound constraining $L\geqα_0 C^{3/4}$ for some constant $α_0$. There is currently an order-of-magnitude range for the value of $α_0$ between 1.105 and 10.76. In this work, we show that T(Q,Q) torus links can be constructed such that the upper bound is within a factor of 1.77 of the lower bound.
